🚂 Transport Dashboard (Rev.130.1)

Trailer / axle line generator
Status: ● Connecting... ✓ Synced

🚂 Generate Trailer

Set Number of trains and Number of Hydraulic Groups at the top of the train list to size the dashboard: e.g. Number of trains = 2 gives you 2 trains, Number of Hydraulic Groups = 3 gives EVERY train 3 axle groups (max 4, since there are only 4 fixed groups). Both are kept in sync with Excel sheet "Input", cells B1 (Number of trains) and B2 (Number of Hydraulic Groups): editing either here writes it straight to Excel, and the ⇩ button pulls the latest value back in and resizes the dashboard to match. Define one or more trailer trains. Axle #1 of each train sits at the entered X offset — the distance from the barge's origin (0,0) to the top-left corner of the trailer; every following axle = previous axle's X − line spacing, all sharing the same Y offset — the distance from origin (0,0) to the top-left corner of the trailer along Y. X offset and Y offset are kept in sync with Excel sheet "Input", cells B5 (X offset) and B6 (Y offset): editing either field here writes it straight to Excel, and the ⇩ button next to each label pulls the latest value back in. New trains start with the same line spacing and X/Y offset as the trailer above them. Split each train's axle-line range into axle groups (e.g. axle lines 1–5 @ 25 t, axle lines 6–10 @ 50 t) and pick one of the 4 fixed groups for each range from the dropdown — or mark a group No line load for axles that carry no cargo weight. For a Goldhofer or SPMT preset trailer, each axle line is really a pair of physical axles (a right axle and a left axle sitting opposite each other) — use each group's Axle row field to apply that group to both axles, the right axle only, or the left axle only, so e.g. a 6-line/12-axle Goldhofer can have columns 1–2 in one group (both rows) while columns 3–6's right axles sit in a second group and their left axles sit in a third. If a train is actually made up of several separate physical SPMT units (e.g. a 10-line train built from a 4-line unit followed by a 6-line unit), use that train's AutoCAD split field to enter the axle-line count per unit, front → back (e.g. 4,6) — each unit then gets its own AutoCAD block insert on export, instead of one block for the whole train; leave it blank for the old one-block-per-train behavior. Rows are written to Load_Editor!B (name, e.g. Group_1_line_1) and D:G starting at row 124 (D = Line load t, E = X, F = Y, G = VCG). "📤 Push to Excel" writes each axle LINE's X/Y position and group number (no load/VCG) to sheet Adjust_Wheels, with axle lines as rows (A4 = Line 1 … A123 = Line 120) and one 6‑column block per train (Train 1 = B:G, Train 2 = H:M, Train 3 = N:S, …: left x-pos/y-pos/Group then right x-pos/y-pos/Group), and in the same click also writes each train's AutoCAD split segments to Input!A11:C30 (row 10 = "Set Train Group"): one row per split segment (or one row for the whole train if AutoCAD split is blank), column A/D/G/… = split type (e.g. GHF 4), and the next two columns = that segment's first axle line's Group Nr for the left and right axle respectively — 3 columns per train, Train 1 = A:C, Train 2 = D:F, and so on through Train 10. The same click also writes each linked train's X offset/Y offset to Input (Train 1 = B5/B6, Train 2 = E5/E6, Train 3 = H5/H6, … through Train 10) — this is the only time those cells are pushed to (they're only ever pulled automatically on panel open/refresh, never on every edit). Adjust_Wheels stores axle-CENTER positions (distance from origin 0,0 to the center of each axle), which is different from X offset/Y offset (distance from 0,0 to the trailer deck's top-left corner) — the preview's dimension callouts show both. "⇩ Refresh from Adjust_Wheels" reads the axle grid back the other way; every linked train's (Train 1-10) X offset/Y offset is then re-linked to its own Input cell pair (Train 1 = B5/B6, Train 2 = E5/E6, Train 3 = H5/H6, … 3 columns apart) rather than left as a raw axle position, so it stays the deck-corner value everywhere. Editing X offset/Y offset on the dashboard is always picked up automatically the next time you push, since nothing is cached. This same read also runs automatically the first time the panel opens (and on every refresh) whenever Adjust_Wheels isn't blank. While reading, each train's Trailer type is auto-detected from the spacing between its axle lines: exactly 1500 mm → Goldhofer, exactly 1400 mm → SPMT (anything else stays Custom / Manual), and its axle-line count is taken directly from how many Line N rows that train's block has in Adjust_Wheels.

📦 Generate Cargo

Up to 5 cargo items, linked to Excel sheet "Input", cells AZ35:BD39 (Name / W [mTe] / X [m] / Y [m] / Z [m]) and BE35:BJ39 (Length [m] / Width [m] / Height [m] / CoG to Left [m] / CoG to Rear [m] / CoG to Bottom [m]) — all in meters, unlike the mm trailer fields above. X and Y are the cargo's Center of Gravity (CoG) distance from world origin (0,0) — the same origin the trailer's X offset/Y offset use, just in meters instead of mm — and Z is the CoG height above the trailer deck. Length, Width, and Height size the box drawn in the preview, and CoG to Left/CoG to Rear/CoG to Bottom position that box — each is the distance from this item's own CoG to the box's left/rear/bottom edge. Editing a CoG field (CoGx/CoGy/CoGz) moves only the CoG sign, and editing a CoG-to-edge field moves only the box — unless the item's 🧲 Group toggle is on, in which case editing CoGx/CoGy/CoGz drags the box along with it (the offsets stay fixed) and every other field on that item is disabled, leaving only CoGx/CoGy/CoGz editable. All of these are pulled/pushed as written in Excel. Pulled automatically when this panel opens or refreshes; press "📤 Push Cargo to Excel" to write changes back (row 40's TOTAL stays a live Excel formula and is never overwritten). Below the cargo list, the 🧲 Group All section lets you nudge every cargo item — CoG sign AND drawn box together — at once: tick its toggle, then edit its own CoGx/CoGy/CoGz fields — each edit applies that same X/Y/Z delta to EVERY cargo item's CoG and box alike (regardless of that item's own individual 🧲 Group toggle), so the whole cargo set — position and shape both — slides together while every item keeps its size and its offsets from its own CoG unchanged. It resets to 0/0/0 each time it's switched on and is local-only (not written to Excel).

🌬 Horizontal Loads

Wind, speed/acceleration, road-gradient, curve, and friction inputs used for the horizontal-load / stability calc, linked to their own Excel sheet "Input horizontal loads": H14 (Centre of Wind height, m), H16 (Operational allowable wind speed, m/s), H18 (Drag coefficient), H20 (Trailer speed, km/h), H21 (Max. acceleration, m/sec²), H22 (Max. deceleration, m/sec²), B23/E23 (Transverse road gradient / inc. stroke compensation, %) with H23 (Gr_trans, deg) as its Excel-computed result, B24/E24 (Longitudinal road gradient / inc. stroke compensation, %) with H24 (Gr_long, deg) as its Excel-computed result, H25 (Curve impact, %), and H26 (Friction Steel/Wood). Every field except H23/H24 (🔒 read-only — Excel computes those) is pulled/pushed like the fields above: pulled automatically when this panel opens or refreshes, on-demand via each field's own ⇩ button, and written back with "📤 Push to Excel" below. The current values are also drawn as a small callout in the plan-view preview, top-right of the origin sign.

📐 CoG Envelope

Reproduces the "CoG_Envelope" reference workbook's Cargo CoG envelope calculation (sheet "2") directly in this dashboard. Cargo Dim. (X/Y/Z, m — workbook C10:E10) is 🔒 pull-only, auto-synced from Excel "Input"!BE{row}/BF{row}/BG{row}. Cargo CoG (X/Y/Z, m — workbook C11:E11) is also 🔒 pull-only, auto-synced from Excel "Input"!BB{row}/BC{row}/BJ{row}. In both cases {row} is whichever cargo item is picked from the 🔽 Cargo Selection dropdown above (synced with "Input"!AZ35:AZ39, defaulting to AZ35). Neither is ever written back to Excel or editable here. Slope shift (uphill LC1&4 / downhill LC2&3, workbook C18/C19) stays a local-only input — no Excel source given for those, so type them in directly; Y/Z have no slope-shift input, matching the workbook's "N/A" there. The table further down (📊 CoG Envelope Table, below 📋 Transport Data) is every downstream formula from that sheet (CoG envelope (5%), load cases LC1–LC4, and the same again with the uphill/downhill slope shift folded in), computed here in the dashboard's own code rather than pulled from Excel.

⚓ Lashing

Sea-fastening lashing TYPE list — one row/group per lashing type, matching the reference workbook "Lashing calculation" sheet (A18:F41 + P18:P41, up to 24 types — the type count follows column A's non-blank rows on pull). Per type: Lashing point (optional — which drawn L# sign(s) this type is installed at, e.g. "L1, L2, L5, L23" or "L3A, L4C, L23D" for SPMT; not case-sensitive (l1 = L1) and a range like "L1-L3" expands to L1, L2, L3; QTY auto-fills to the count once you type any — synced with column P, so it survives a pull the same as SWL/QTY/dx/dy/dz do. Can also be set by clicking an L# sign directly in the 2D top/side/end views below — that toggles the clicked sign into whichever type's card is currently "active" (click a card, or focus any of its fields, to make it the active one). A dot that stands for several points (SPMT, e.g. L1A/L1D) steps on each click through: none → all of them together (L1A, L1D) → L1A → L1D → none, SWL (Safe Working Load of one lashing/chain of this type, mTe), QTY (number of identical lashings of this type), and dx / dy / dz (mm — offset from the cargo attachment point to the deck/lashing-eye anchor point, same for every point listed under "Lashing point"). Length, alfa, beta, and the capacity / Unity Check columns are genuine Excel formulas in the reference sheet now — see the read-only Lashing calculation table under 🚚 Transport Data w/ CoG Env for those. Synced with Excel: pushes/pulls A18:F41 (column A's "No." is written by this dashboard as a plain position number, not an Excel formula — removing a type clears its whole row, No. included) and P18:P41 (Lashing point). Unlike the other cards, this one does not auto-push on every edit — fields turn amber the moment you change them and stay that way until you press "📤 Push to Excel" below, which also pulses amber while the push is in flight, then flashes green/red.

L# signs (2D drawing): placed automatically from each train's own deck length/width and type (Goldhofer/SPMT) — NOT from the rows above. First sign 1500 mm (Goldhofer) / 700 mm (SPMT) from the FRONT edge of the top deck, then every 1500 mm / 1400 mm toward the rear, on both long edges, never past the rear edge. Numbered clockwise from the Right side (front→rear, L1..Ln) then the Left side (rear→front, L{n+1}..L{2n}) — e.g. a 14AL Goldhofer draws L1-L13 on the Right, L14-L26 on the Left. For SPMT, each station is a 4-point bracket — L#A (Top-Front), L#B (Top-Rear), L#C (Bottom-Rear), L#D (Bottom-Front), 480 mm front↔rear, 210 mm top↔bottom, centered on the station's own X. Shown as small dots in Top View (Goldhofer: one dot/side/station; SPMT: two, front and rear), Side View (dots wherever two points coincide once Y collapses, joined "/"-labeled), and both end views (Front/Rear View — composite range dots per side, e.g. "L1-L13", doubled top+bottom for SPMT) — every one of these dots is clickable (see above). The totals line below flags if the drawn sign count doesn't match the QTY sum above — the two are independent by design (QTY is physical lashing hardware count for the capacity calc; L# signs are the deck layout), so a mismatch is just informational, not an error.

📋 Transport Data

Read-only mirror of Excel sheet "Drawing_table" — pulled, never pushed (the sheet's own values are Excel-computed). Pressing a 📤 button in the 📊 CoG Envelope Table below updates the TRANSPORT TABLE header above to name that load case (e.g. TRANSPORT TABLE LC0 or TRANSPORT TABLE LC1-Slope) and mirrors this table's data to Excel — plain-section rows to sheet "Drawing_table_LC", with-slope rows (LC1-Slope–LC4-Slope) to the separate sheet "Drawing_table_LC_Slope" — each in that load case's own column block, keeping a separate snapshot per load case in its own sheet.

📊 CoG Envelope Table

Same layout as the "CoG_Envelope" reference workbook (sheet "2"!C8:E24) — computed live in this dashboard's own code from the 📐 CoG Envelope fields above, using the workbook's exact formulas. The table (row labels only, dash-filled) is visible as soon as this panel opens; press 🧮 Calculate CoG Envelope below to fill in, show, and auto-push the numeric X/Y/Z/Z-from-top-deck data to Excel "Check CASE A & CASE B"!B67:E73 (CoG envelope section) and B75:E81 (with-slope section) — the row labels already in column A and the two section banners are left untouched. The Z (From trailer top deck) column is only populated for CARGO CoG. In Axis-LC0 and the LC1–LC4 rows (both sections) — everywhere else it's N/A, same as the reference workbook. The with-slope section's own LC1–LC4 rows are labelled LC1-Slope, LC2-Slope, LC3-Slope and LC4-Slope to keep them visually distinct from the plain section above. Each CARGO CoG. In Axis-LC0, LC1–LC4, and LC1-Slope–LC4-Slope row has its own small 📤 button that pushes just that load case's X/Y and its Z (From trailer top deck) — NOT the plain local Z — to "Input"!BB35:BD35 — the same cells the rest of the workbook's transport table calculates the active cargo CoG from — updates the TRANSPORT TABLE header in 📋 Transport Data above to name that load case (e.g. TRANSPORT TABLE LC1 or TRANSPORT TABLE LC1-Slope), refreshes 📋 Transport Data so that load case's transport table shows immediately, and mirrors the same data to Excel — kept STRICTLY separate by section: CARGO CoG. In Axis-LC0 and plain LC1–LC4 rows mirror to sheet "Drawing_table_LC", in that load case's own column block (LC0/LC1/LC2/LC3/LC4 side by side); LC1-Slope–LC4-Slope rows mirror instead to a separate sheet "Drawing_table_LC_Slope", in its own LC1-Slope/LC2-Slope/LC3-Slope/LC4-Slope column block — never both.

📈 CoG Envelope Summary

Read-only mirror of UNITY CHECK / MAX GBP / STABILITY CHECK rows across every load case — pulled, never pushed. Static comes from sheet "Drawing_table" for the MAX GBP row, and from sheet "Drawing_table_LC"!D56:D62 for the 7 STABILITY rows; LC0–LC4 come from sheet "Drawing_table_LC" (each load case's own column block); LC1-Slope–LC4-Slope (MAX GBP row only) come from sheet "Drawing_table_LC_Slope". The Unit column is a fixed label ([mTe/m²] for MAX GBP, [deg] for the STABILITY rows) — not a pulled value. Deliberately does not sync with the 📊 CoG Envelope Table above — this pulls independently, the same way 📋 Transport Data does. Any UNITY CHECK or MAX GBP value over 1 is highlighted red, the same way DETAIL CHECK REQUIRED rows are in 📋 Transport Data above — but for the STABILITY rows it's the opposite: those are flagged red when they fall under 1, since a smaller stability angle means less margin. The Static column itself is shown plainly and is never flagged.

🚚 Transport Data w/ CoG Env

4 read-only tables — TRANSPORT TABLE LC1 through TRANSPORT TABLE LC4 — in the exact same style as 📋 Transport Data above. Each one is pulled from its own column block in Excel sheet "Drawing_table_LC" (LC1 at column AA, LC2 at BA, LC3 at CA, LC4 at DA — the same blocks a 📤 button in 📊 CoG Envelope Table writes to), so once every load case has been pushed at least once, all 4 tables here show their own permanent snapshot side by side. Pull-only, never pushed. Auto-refreshes right after 🧮 Calculate CoG Envelope finishes its full push/refresh sequence (📊 CoG Envelope Table push, then 📈 CoG Envelope Summary refresh, then every load case's own mirror into "Drawing_table_LC") — no need to press its own refresh button separately after that. This is also exactly what the 📐 AutoCAD export below uses for its own LC1-4 quadrant tables, so the exported .scr matches what's shown here.
